posts.author: KravenarGames
posts.body:
Okay, Let me share some light, after a deep inspection.
Upgrade NWJS to last 102 version -> Possible.
Upgrade PixiJS to last version? Not possible (or, better to say, you can do it but it's pointless).
The max version supported is 7.x. (I did that on MV)
Results? Even more lag. LOL
NWJS is basically Chrome sandboxed, it doesn't have access to real drivers.
So we can forget about WebGpu and WebGL, the only thing that will work will always be the
Canvas Rendering . - aka - can't reach proper performance ever in this life.
Oh, and, you can use Canvas rendering if you code your own software rendering system, because they removed the Canvas Rendering from the library, that means... no fallback -> Persistant Black Screen.
Unless... someone would compile from the scratch NWJS to un-sandbox it, and let it access to the system.
It took me two days of tests and inspections.
You're welcome.
P.s. there are workarounds of course, like forgetting about NWJS and use another embedding system but since we cannot customize the editor, and neither the export process.. is really worth it to complicate our life with that? Meh.

posts.author: KravenarGames
posts.body:
Ok so far, I've found a way that PIxi8 could be achieved.
It's not easy.
Basically, it includes editing the calls that the core makes to pixi and create a kind of compatibility layer for the whole graphic system.
CORE -> Layer -> Pixi
This way, all pixi calls goes through the layer, and the layer "talks" to PIXI, so with this layer the upgrade to future pixi version becomes easy because just one file needs to be touched, and with some workaround the canvas could be re-created.
Apparently, with some flags is possible to force direct redenring (disabling fallback), so maybe the Webgpu could be achieved.
I'm going to go through this deep road. LOL

posts.author: KravenarGames
posts.body:
Update 1
​
This is the current problem with RMV\RMZ:
In the normal core: the renderer is created manually.
Pixi7 supports the handling for the canvas render directly from PIXI.Application, which is synchronous (ad rpg maker), while Pixi8 has the the Application asynchronous, which means is based on a "await until ready"-kind system.
So yeah, in the end, a whole boot system needs to be re-written.
Already porting pixi-tilemap to Pixi 7 was a hell, this will require some time.
Note: The problem between the rendertype (limited WebGL and WebGPU) may be in the way the system creates manually the render stage. Since it's manually creating, that could be the reason why WebGPU doesn't work.
Update 2
​
I've converted the core to esm (ES2020), and noticed that plugins stopped working (apparently overriding functions is problematic\not smooth and easy with esm), so now I got back to the normal js files.
I'm going to try to rely directly on PIXI for the render\stage system and see what will happen.
Going for another night of coding.
Update 3
​
I've found out that RM has an internal ticker system.
Relying on the pixi one, I got +XXXX FPS. LMFAO.
The game was unplayable.
-> TO THE MOON! Hahah.
What I found out: They capped voluntarily the FPS to 60 using a "wait anim" system.
Last Update
​
Tests done:
-
Delegating completely the render to PIXI 8
-
Delegating completely the tick system to the PIXI's internal system.
Results:
- Gameplay: same, scene_manager needed to be adjusted.
- Menus: FPS drops in menus
- Conclusion: unstability
everywhere
.
Final conclusion
: after a whole rewrite of almost everything: Pixi 8 isn't worth it.
Reasons:
-
No difference seen with pixi 7 in performance
- A lot of headaches to implement things since they are based on promises calls (await \ promise)
- Some performance are even worst (lag\stuttering\etc) even with capped FPS 60\120 (WebGL, not WebGPU)
- To make it work flawlessly, a whole engine re-write is needed, since now is all synchronous, and pixi 8 works with asynchronous ways.
It would take an infinite amount of time\coding and in the end the outcoming result is even not worth it (performance drops). Whatever they (the pixi guys) achieved, is totally not work-able with the whole rpg maker engine flow\system.

This is the compatibility layer working for PIxiJS7 (last version).
You could put it after loading pixi (and libs) in your index.html, and
BEFORE
loading the Rpg maker core JS files.
Of course, you'll need to migrate all the PIXI calls from the core files (Class graphics, etc.) to this compat layer, but so far, it's working like a charm.
The most stable library to use today is PixiJS7.
Going for PixiJS 8 will require a whole engine rewrite plus definitely a new\decent editor that will support autoupgrade of nwjs, which is something that I could do (the editor) in Python (to have it multi-os compatibile), if and when I'll have some free time.
If I'll ever do that, I'll push it online as free, editor included.
Now, about my compat layer.
The thing is easy:
Everything where is used in plain PIXI, you should use core_gfx.
So core_gfx will be the "interpreter" between the core and PIXI, this way, if some ever update will be needed, we'll need to touch
a single short file
instead of +10k lines files.
Note: I've added also the ported pixi-tilemap.
If you'll rely on the compat-layer Pixi-picture won't be needed anymore, every call is handled natively by coregfx. These two are compatibile with both MV\MZ. I'm on MV, but tested on MZ works as well.

Totally agree with what
@KravenarGames
mentioned earlier—optimization usually has a bigger impact on FPS than just upgrading the rendering engine. The main bottleneck is that RPG Maker is still heavy on CPU calculations, barely touching the GPU where Pixi actually shines.
However,
WebGPU
is the real game-changer here. It makes the effort worth it because it essentially "forces" the engine to utilize Pixi’s features more optimally during refactoring.
My workflow is a bit different from the usual "Optimize-> Port" method.
Instead, I do: Port to next Pixi -> Optimize.
(This makes bug tracing much easier since the codebase stays familiar).
As for compatibility: It’s surprisingly stable! My port barely breaks existing plugins. I even wrote a custom wrapper so that the default NW.js v0.48.4 in MZ works like magic with Pixi v8.
P.S. I'm actually taking it a step further by
porting MV to
Tauri
. You get WebGPU support and a runtime size of just
1 MB
(vs hundreds of MB with NW.js).
You can visit the GitHub project link in my signature.
Please note that as of this writing, I've only pushed the update up to Pixi v7.

posts.author: RyanBram
posts.body:
TheAM-Dol said:
@RyanBram
I'm interested in parts of your project, but I have concerns about AI usage in it's development, especially given the way the description has been written.
Was AI used in part or wholly in the development of your project? Could you disclose that?
Click to expand...
Thanks for asking! I appreciate the opportunity to clarify this.
To be fully transparent: Yes, I utilize AI, but primarily
as a research assistant and for documentation.
1. The Code & Logic:
I used AI to analyze the documentation and internal code differences between Pixi versions to spot syntax changes. However, the architectural decisions were 100% manual myself.
Proof of this is in the code structure: If AI were fully in control, it would likely rewrite the RPG Maker core into modern ES syntax to match Pixi v8 standards. Instead, I made a
conscious human decision
to strictly maintain ES5 syntax (using
Object.assign
, etc.). This ensures legacy plugins remain compatible and the engine works on older NW.js runtimes.
2. Why AI was necessary:
Finding human assistance for this specific port is
nearly impossible, even within the Pixi community
. To do this effectively, one needs deep knowledge of
both
Pixi internals and RPG Maker's unique architecture. While frameworks like Phaser are common knowledge there, RPG Maker MV is widely different and quite niche. Since finding a human with this specific intersection of skills is extremely rare, I used AI to help bridge that specific knowledge gap.
3. Documentation & Efficiency:
Since English isn't my first language, I use AI to polish my drafts. Honestly, it’s a massive time-saver. It allows me to focus my mental energy on
coding and development
rather than getting stuck on writing perfect grammar.
Hope that clears things up!
jackass__ said:
So it's also compatible with MZ ? you mentionned a custom wrapper that works with MZ and Pixi v8
Click to expand...
To clarify regarding MZ compatibility:
The wrapper I mentioned earlier allows this engine to run smoothly on the
NW.js version used by MZ
, but fully porting the
MZ Core Script
itself to Pixi v8 is a different beast. I'm avoiding touching the MZ Core specifically for two reasons:
Active Maintenance:
Unlike MV, MZ is still actively maintained and updated by KADOKAWA.
Licensing:
MZ is not explicitly Open Source. This is a huge contrast to the MV Core Script, which is strictly
MIT Licensed
and openly encourages community support (Source:
GitHub - rpgtkoolmv/corescript
).
However, here is the good news:
Instead of porting MZ directly, I am working on implementing MZ-like features
into this MV port
.
My goal is to recreate the MZ experience (mechanically) within this MIT-licensed MV engine, without lifting/using a single line of MZ's proprietary code. Best of both worlds!
Thank you.

mentioned earlier—optimization usually has a bigger impact on FPS than just upgrading the rendering engine. The main bottleneck is that RPG Maker is still heavy on CPU calculations, barely touching the GPU where Pixi actually shines.
However,
WebGPU
is the real game-changer here. It makes the effort worth it because it essentially "forces" the engine to utilize Pixi’s features more optimally during refactoring.
My workflow is a bit different from the usual "Optimize-> Port" method.
Instead, I do: Port to next Pixi -> Optimize.
(This makes bug tracing much easier since the codebase stays familiar).
As for compatibility: It’s surprisingly stable! My port barely breaks existing plugins. I even wrote a custom wrapper so that the default NW.js v0.48.4 in MZ works like magic with Pixi v8.
P.S. I'm actually taking it a step further by
porting MV to
Tauri
. You get WebGPU support and a runtime size of just
1 MB
(vs hundreds of MB with NW.js).
You can visit the GitHub project link in my signature.
Please note that as of this writing, I've only pushed the update up to Pixi v7.
Click to expand...
What about just turning off the every-frame-check for parallaxes and making it using only in maps where actually parallaxes are present? It increases x10 the fps. LOL
Note: WebGPU requires drivers to have a valid passthrough (last nwjs + os that supports current driver correctly). That means breaking the compatibility with Cordova (Android) and Linux (mostly because if you're not on AMD not all NWJS deals happily with Nvidia on Linux - Wayland). So, it's not really about the rendering engine, it's about how the core ticks internally to define the FPS and use power. With few small tweaks you can achieve definitely a lot remaining still on Pixi. Tested.

posts.body:
I did see Pixiv8 for MZ from Japan:
https://booth.pm/en/items/7147423
I haven't personally tried it but I thought it might interest people but I do have it. It gives you a 40 page manual and here are some of the information. I can only give a summary as the author doesn't allow manual distribution?
Code:
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
WHAT IS MOREPIXI?
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
MorePixi is a complete rewrite of RPG Maker MZ's core scripts that upgrades 
PixiJS from v5 to v8.13.2. It's NOT a regular plugin - it replaces the entire 
core script system.

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
REQUIREMENTS
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
• PIXI: v8.13.2
• NW.js: Default for MZ core script version 1.9.0
• ⚠️ EXISTING MZ PLUGINS WILL NOT WORK - They need to be rewritten for MP

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
INSTALLATION
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
1. Backup these files in your project (rename them):
   - js/main.js
   - js/libs/pixi.js

2. Copy the included js folder into your project's js folder

3. Files installed:
   - js/libs/pixi.js (new PixiJS v8)
   - js/main.js (modified loader)
   - js/mp_core.js (replaces rmmz_core.js)
   - js/mp_managers.js (replaces rmmz_managers.js)
   - js/mp_sprites.js (replaces rmmz_sprites.js)
   - js/mp_objects.js (replaces rmmz_objects.js)
   - js/mp_scenes.js (replaces rmmz_scenes.js)
   - js/mp_windows.js (replaces rmmz_windows.js)

⚠️ If you use "Update Core Script" in the editor, you'll need to reinstall!

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
KEY CHANGES FOR PLUGIN DEVELOPERS
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------

1. NO MORE BITMAP CLASS
   // MZ (old)
   sp.bitmap = ImageManager.loadPicture("Actor1_1");
   
   // MP (new)
   sp.loadTextureAsync("img/pictures/Actor1_1.png");

2. UPDATE → tUPDATE
   // MZ (old)
   MyClass.prototype.update = function() { ... }
   
   // MP (new)  
   MyClass.prototype.tUpdate = function() { ... }

3. ASYNC FUNCTIONS END WITH "Async"
   // MZ (old)
   DataManager.loadDatabase();
   
   // MP (new)
   DataManager.loadDatabaseAsync();

4. CLASS SYNTAX REQUIRED FOR DERIVED CLASSES
   // MZ (old)
   function MyScene() { this.initialize(...arguments); }
   MyScene.prototype = Object.create(Scene_Base.prototype);
   
   // MP (new)
   class MyScene extends Scene_Base { }

5. PROMISES INSTEAD OF CALLBACKS
   // MZ (old)
   sp.bitmap.addLoadListener((bitmap) => { ... });
   
   // MP (new)
   sp.loadTextureAsync(src).then((texture) => { ... });

6. WINDOW SKIN SIMPLIFIED
   // MZ (old)
   this.windowskin = ImageManager.loadSystem("Window2");
   
   // MP (new)
   this.windowskin = "Window2";

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
NEW CLASSES
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
• CanvasSprite - For direct canvas drawing (replaces Bitmap drawing)
• BackgroundSprite - For scene background snapshots
• Sprite_Snap - For capturing containers/sprites to texture
• TextureManager - New texture caching system (replaces ImageManager for textures)
• Container_Clickable - Clickable container for button creation
• Sprite_Parallax - For parallax/battle backgrounds
• Window_ScrollTextEx - Message-independent scroll text

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
NOTABLE FEATURES
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
• Textures are now shared between sprites (better memory usage)
• Weather effects work in battle scenes too
• MV animations can be imported (put [mv] in animation name)
• Multiple symbols can be mapped to one key
• Automatic text line-break functions added
• FPS counter removed from release builds (use FpsViewer.js plugin if needed)

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
WARNINGS
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
⚠️ This is NOT a finished product
⚠️ NO SUPPORT is provided by the author
⚠️ Existing MZ plugins WILL NOT work without modification
⚠️ Use at your own risk
And some more information:
• PIXI_v8 has several memory leak issues reported, so when using PIXI items independently, it's good to use heap snapshots to check.
• If a specific PIXI object increases by the same number each time you repeat instance creation and destruction, try adjusting destroy().
•  It also depends on GC timing, so after thinking "it's increasing", wait a bit and retake the heap. During MP development, there were often false alarms. (ParticleContainer might also be nothing to worry about)

I have archived all the core RPG Maker files here:
https://github.com/RyanBram/RPG-MV-Ace/tree/main/archive

Pixi v7 is the most stable so far, but it hasn't undergone optimization yet because I was focused on upgrading Pixi before optimization. My plan is to optimize Pixi v7, add many built-in features to make it easier for users, and then revisit my Pixi v8.

https://ryanbram.github.io/RPGMV-Ace/

RyanBram
